meta.name: Send daily AI market briefings to Telegram, Discord and Postgres with OpenAI, Twelve Data, CoinGecko, FRED, QuantGist and Marketaux

name: AI Morning Market Briefing with Vendor-Neutral AI Agent, PostgreSQL, Telegram & Discord

parameters.content:
## Daily AI Market Briefing

### How it works

This workflow creates a weekday market briefing from multiple structured data sources. It collects cross-asset market data from Twelve Data and CoinGecko, the US 10-year Treasury yield from FRED, macro events from QuantGist, and market news from Marketaux. Each source is normalized before the data is merged and checked for missing or failed inputs. An AI model then produces a structured market briefing, which is validated and formatted for delivery. The final report can be sent to Telegram and Discord and stored in PostgreSQL for later use.

### Setup

- Add credentials for Twelve Data, CoinGecko, FRED, QuantGist, and Marketaux.
- Open Setup Workflow Configuration and set the report timezone and AI model metadata.
- Connect a compatible AI chat model to the briefing agent.
- Configure Telegram, Discord, and PostgreSQL credentials as needed.
- Disable or remove any delivery branch you do not plan to use.
- If using PostgreSQL, create the required `public.briefings` table first.
- Run the workflow once manually, then activate the schedule.
### Customization

Adjust the schedule, report timezone, tracked assets, data sources, AI model, or delivery channels to match your reporting needs.

## Schedule and configuration

Starts the workflow on weekdays and provides the shared report settings used downstream.

## Fetch and normalize data

Collects and normalizes five market, macro, and news data sources before merging.

## Merge and prepare data

Combines normalized sources, records source health, and prepares the payload for AI analysis.

## Generate and validate briefing

Creates the structured AI market briefing and validates the final output schema.

## Telegram delivery

Formats the briefing for Telegram and sends the final message.

## Database storage

Builds the database insert and stores the full briefing in PostgreSQL.

## Discord delivery

Builds a Discord embed and sends the market briefing.

parameters.jsCode: const expected=['twelve_data','coingecko','fred','quantgist','marketaux']; const sources={}; for(const item of $input.all()){const v=item.json||{}; if(v.source) sources[v.source]={status:v.status||'invalid',data:v.data??null,error:v.error??null,core:Boolean(v.core)};} for(const s of expected) if(!sources[s]) sources[s]={status:'error',data:null,error:'Source branch produced no result',core:['twelve_data','coingecko','fred'].includes(s)}; const failures=Object.entries(sources).filter(([s,v])=>['twelve_data','coingecko','fred'].includes(s)&&v.status!=='ok').map(([source,v])=>({source,status:v.status,error:v.error})); return [{json:{normalized_sources:sources,source_health:Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(sources).map(([s,v])=>[s,{status:v.status,error:v.error,core:v.core}])),core_source_failures:failures,all_sources_completed:expected.every(s=>sources[s])}}];

parameters.text:
=You are a disciplined financial market analyst. Analyze ONLY the supplied normalized source data and return a detailed morning market briefing in English as valid JSON.

CORE RULES
- Never invent prices, percentage moves, events, forecasts, actual values, news, or causes.
- Clearly distinguish observed facts from interpretation.
- If data is missing, stale, partial, invalid, or unavailable, say so briefly and do not guess.
- Never claim that a headline or macro event caused a market move unless the supplied data directly supports that conclusion.
- When causality is uncertain, use careful language such as "may be related", "is in focus", or "is a potential driver".
- The FULL structured analysis is for PostgreSQL. Do not artificially shorten the JSON because Telegram has a message limit; the Telegram formatter handles that separately.
- All human-readable fields must be in English.
- Return ONLY valid JSON. No markdown code fence and no text outside the JSON.

MARKET / RATES RULES
- market_regime MUST be exactly one of: risk_on, mild_risk_on, neutral, mild_risk_off, risk_off.
- TLT is the price of a long-duration US Treasury ETF. Do not confuse bond prices with yields.
- Discuss the US 10Y yield only from the FRED input.
- If TLT and US10Y appear inconsistent or one is stale, describe them separately and mention freshness where relevant.
- Use the supplied asset data to identify cross-asset confirmation or divergence, but do not overstate it.

MACRO
- events_today should contain only events relevant to the current date.
- Prioritize CPI, PPI, PCE, NFP, unemployment, GDP, FOMC, ECB, HICP, ISM and retail sales.
- If actual / forecast / previous is absent, keep it null.
- Use the configured report timezone for all human-readable event times in watch_next.
- Upcoming high-impact events should appear in watch_next.

NEWS
- Select at most 3 genuinely market-relevant supplied headlines.
- Prefer macro, rates, major indices, mega-cap/sector developments, commodities, geopolitics and systemically relevant companies.
- Company-specific news should be included only when it plausibly matters to a broad index, sector, risk sentiment or a tracked asset.
- Never invent content beyond the supplied title/description/context.
- If no supplied article is important enough, return top_news as [].

SOURCE INPUT SHAPE
- CoinGecko supplies only USD price, 24-hour percentage change, and last update time for each tracked crypto asset.
- QuantGist supplies a compact event list containing only title/label, country, release time, impact, actual, forecast, previous, and release status.

OUTPUT CONSISTENCY
- watch_next MUST be an array of plain strings only.
- Do not return duplicate or near-duplicate news items covering the same story.
- Do not add alternate field names such as current_price, value, change, driver, area, or scheduled_time; use the requested schema exactly.

DETAIL LEVEL FOR THE FULL REPORT
- headline: concise and informative.
- summary: 4-6 useful sentences.
- drivers: 3-5 items. Each should have a specific title and a 1-3 sentence evidence-based explanation.
- opportunities: 2-4 items ONLY when justified. Each needs a specific name, thesis, catalyst, risk, invalidation and horizon. Never use a generic name such as "Opportunity".
- watch_next: 3-6 concrete items explaining what to watch and why.
- missing_sources: short human-readable data notes, not verbose internal diagnostics.
DATA FRESHNESS RULES
- Account for weekends and market holidays when judging freshness.
- On Saturday, Sunday, or before the next regular trading session, the latest Friday close is expected and must NOT be described as stale or incomplete merely because it predates the briefing timestamp.
- FRED series may publish with a normal reporting lag. Mention the observation date only when that lag materially affects interpretation.
- Do not create multiple data notes for the same missing input.
- If the macro calendar contains no events, state this once only.
- missing_sources should contain only actionable or interpretation-relevant limitations, not routine timing differences.

Current configured report time:
{{ $now.setZone($('Setup Workflow Configuration').first().json.report_timezone).toISO() }}

NORMALIZED SOURCES:
{{ JSON.stringify($('Prepare Data for AI Model').item.json.normalized_sources) }}

SOURCE HEALTH:
{{ JSON.stringify($('Prepare Data for AI Model').item.json.source_health) }}

CORE FAILURES:
{{ JSON.stringify($('Prepare Data for AI Model').item.json.core_source_failures) }}

Return exactly these top-level fields:
{
  "generated_at": "ISO timestamp",
  "market_regime": "risk_on|mild_risk_on|neutral|mild_risk_off|risk_off",
  "headline": "string",
  "summary": "string",
  "missing_sources": ["string"],
  "assets": [
    {
      "symbol": "string",
      "price": "string or number",
      "change_percent": null,
      "direction": "up|down|flat",
      "signal": "green|yellow|orange|red",
      "comment": "string"
    }
  ],
  "events_today": [
    {
      "time": "string",
      "event": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "importance": "high|medium|low",
      "previous": null,
      "forecast": null,
      "actual": null,
      "status": "upcoming|released",
      "comment": "string"
    }
  ],
  "top_news": [
    {
      "title": "string",
      "source": "string",
      "published_at": "string",
      "url": "string",
      "relevance": "string"
    }
  ],
  "drivers": [
    {
      "title": "string",
      "explanation": "string",
      "impact": "positive|mixed|negative"
    }
  ],
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "name": "specific setup/theme",
      "thesis": "string",
      "catalyst": "string",
      "risk": "string",
      "invalidation": "string",
      "horizon": "string"
    }
  ],
  "watch_next": ["string"],
  "disclaimer": "Informational analysis only, not individualized financial advice."
}

parameters.jsCode: const b=$input.first().json; const q=v=>v==null?'NULL':"'"+String(v).replace(/'/g,"''")+"'"; const j=v=>q(JSON.stringify(v??null))+'::jsonb'; const vals=[b.generated_at?q(b.generated_at)+'::timestamptz':'NOW()',q(b.market_regime),q(b.headline),q(b.summary),j(b.assets),j(b.events_today),j(b.top_news),j(b.drivers),j(b.opportunities),j(b.watch_next),j(b.raw_sources),q(b.model_provider),q(b.model_name)]; return [{json:{query:'INSERT INTO public.briefings (generated_at,market_regime,headline,summary,assets,events_today,top_news,drivers,opportunities,watch_next,raw_sources,model_provider,model_name) VALUES ('+vals.join(',')+');'}}];
